penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: Ad-free curated social/content feed is a consumer subscription product that requires thousands of paying users to generate meaningful revenue — a solo operator cannot reach that scale through approved outreach channels alone.

rationale: The buyer here is a broad consumer — 'adult professionals frustrated by social media' — which is one of the weakest possible ICPs for a solo B2B factory: no budget authority, very low software purchase intent, and the product requires massive scale to generate revenue. Willingness to pay is weak despite the one commenter's stated intent: Artifact raised millions and shut down, Flipboard and Feedly exist and struggle, and most consumers default to free. There is no realistic path for a solo non-technical operator to build a compelling social feed product and acquire thousands of paying users. Total of 3.3 is well below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: Not recommended. A paid ad-free social/content feed is a consumer media product that requires significant content curation infrastructure, distribution at scale (thousands of paid subscribers to be viable), and differentiation from well-funded incumbents who have already failed (Artifact) or stagnated (Feedly). A solo non-technical operator using a Claude factory cannot realistically build, sell, or sustain this — the b2c_at_scale_needed penalty reflects that the economics only work at a subscriber count that outreach-based acquisition cannot reach. Drop this opportunity.
notes: Failing build gates: buyer_clarity=3 (below floor of 6), willingness_to_pay=3 (below floor of 5), operational_autonomy=6 (meets floor marginally). Total 3.3 is far below min_total_to_validate (5.5). The single-commenter source and broad consumer target make this a weak signal overall.
